title: Variance of a normalized coordinate sign
statement: For every natural number $n$ and every coordinate $i$ among the $n$ coordinates, consider a uniformly random point $X$ of the $n$-dimensional sign cube and the random variable $Y=n^{-1/2}X_i$. Its variance is $n^{-1}$.
hypotheses_covered: $i$ is a coordinate in the dimension-$n$ cube
caveat: At $n=0$, the formal normalization uses the inverse square root of zero; the statement is retained as written, though the displayed simplified value $n^{-1}$ is not defined there.
